tool_args.rationale: The response is monotone-concave, with a broad s_grad span, but s_grad rises alongside u_now in every row. A high-s_grad regime measurement can help separate sink inhibition from input saturation before committing to a quantitative law.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a source-siphon model (nodes C/D) now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The five observations show monotone concavity, but input and sink gradient co-vary; this does not cleanly distinguish sink inhibition from saturation plus a branch term.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the cooperative Hill-inhibition model (node Q) now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: It has four fitted parameters and only five observations, leaving little evidence to discriminate it from other sink-coupled models.
The observed inputs and signatures do not indicate a coupled-memory ODE; this batch is not the most relevant discriminator.
